output:
### Summary

I reviewed commit 10d228d (the four listed files, read in full, plus the diff against origin/main) through a security lens, and ran experiments on a `git archive HEAD` copy in `/tmp/bo-secrev.0MPqJG`. The `tests/run` change is sound: criterion 1 holds both ways, the harness test kills 7 of 7 mutants, and I found no path by which a secret reaches the kept dirs or the CI artifact. The CI half is the weak part. The upload step has never executed (the branch is not on the remote, and the last 8 runs were all green), and the evidence says it will fail when it first runs: scenario `22-dirty-tree` leaves a file whose name contains a line feed, and the pinned `actions/upload-artifact@v4` rejects any such path before uploading anything. I could not run the action end to end (the permission classifier denied executing it locally), so that finding is rated MEDIUM rather than HIGH per the review rules; it should be treated as HIGH once one red CI run confirms it. No CRITICAL or HIGH findings. Nothing here is a vulnerability in the usual sense; the findings are an unexercised and probably broken diagnostics step, a mutable action tag, and robustness gaps around the keep dir.

**Newly added dependency:** `actions/upload-artifact@v4` — a mutable major tag, not a commit SHA. Today it resolves to `ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02`, declares `runs.using: node20`, and is three majors behind the current release (v7.0.2, 2026-10-07). No other dependency is added (`mv`/`mkdir` are coreutils already in use).

### Findings

#### CRITICAL

None.

#### HIGH

None. (See the first MEDIUM: it is HIGH on confirmation.)

#### MEDIUM

- **The upload step will fail on a red run: `22-dirty-tree` leaves a file with a line feed in its name, which upload-artifact@v4 rejects**
  - **Location:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:43-48`; cause at `tests/22-dirty-tree.sh:123`
  - **Description:** `22-dirty-tree.sh:123` creates `test-<pid>-newline/notes\n.txt` and never removes it (the only `rm` in the scenario is line 62, for `zz.txt`). With `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP` set, that file is kept under `22-dirty-tree/cwd/`. `tests/run` runs every scenario regardless of earlier failures, so the file is present on any red run unless `22-dirty-tree` itself dies before line 123. upload-artifact at the pinned SHA validates every file path and throws on `"`, `:`, `<`, `>`, `|`, `*`, `?`, `\r`, `\n` (`dist/upload/index.js:3356-3404`), called per file at line 3684 from `getUploadZipSpecification` at line 3528, before the backend token is read at line 3533. The throw fails the step and uploads nothing, so the feature delivers no artifact in the case it exists for.
  - **What I measured:** a fixture scenario replicating line 123 run with `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP` produced a kept tree of 6 entries, 1 of which has a line feed in its path (`22-dirty-tree/cwd/test-1-newline/notes\n.txt`, confirmed with `od -c`). The rejection is read from source, not executed.
  - **Not reproduced:** the action failing on GitHub. Running `node dist/upload/index.js` locally against a simulated tree was denied by the permission classifier, and I did not retry. To confirm, either push a throwaway commit that makes one scenario fail and read the upload step, or run this (it stops at path validation, before any network call):
    `env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin INPUT_NAME=blast-off-tests INPUT_PATH=/tmp/bo-secrev.0MPqJG/x/knl 'INPUT_IF-NO-FILES-FOUND=warn' 'INPUT_INCLUDE-HIDDEN-FILES=false' INPUT_OVERWRITE=false 'INPUT_COMPRESSION-LEVEL=6' node /tmp/bo-secrev.0MPqJG/ua/index.js`
  - **Suggested fix:** tar the keep dir in a `run:` step under `if: failure()` and upload the single tarball. That is immune to any filename a scenario invents, keeps symlinks as symlinks, and keeps hidden files. Removing the file at the end of `22-dirty-tree` fixes today's case only.

- **The upload step has never run, and its action targets a deprecated runtime**
  - **Location:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:45`
  - **Description:** `git ls-remote --heads origin 'feat/br-1115-issues/*'` returns nothing and the 8 most recent runs all concluded `success`, so the `if: failure()` step has executed 0 times. Run 43778239611 carries the annotation "Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/checkout@v4". `upload-artifact@v4`'s `action.yml` says `using: 'node20'`; v6 says `node24`. The step's first execution will be on a red gate, on a forced runtime it was not built for. Nothing checks criterion 2 mechanically.
  - **Suggested fix:** move to a node24 release (v6 or v7), and exercise the step once before merge (a `workflow_dispatch` run on a branch with a deliberately failing scenario).

- **A keep-dir failure after the first scenario aborts the gate with no verdict line**
  - **Location:** `tests/run:18-19` and `tests/run:34`
  - **Description:** the comment on line 18 promises that a bad keep dir "fails here, not after the suite ran". That holds only for a dir that cannot be created. With an existing, unwritable keep dir: scenario 1 ran, `mv` failed, the script exited 1 under `set -e`, 1 of 3 scenarios ran, no `GATE:` line was printed, and 1 work dir was left in `TMPDIR`. With a stale kept dir that cannot be removed: 2 of 3 scenarios ran, same outcome. It fails closed (exit 1), but it breaks the header's "ends with one verdict line" and turns a diagnostics option into a truncated gate. A full disk in CI takes the same path.
  - **Suggested fix:** probe writability up front (create and remove a temp entry in `$KEEP`), and make a failed keep non-fatal: warn, fall back to `rm -rf "$work"`, continue.

#### LOW

- **Action pinned to a mutable tag** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml:45` (and pre-existing `actions/checkout@v4`, line 16). A moved tag runs new code with the job's token. Blast radius is limited: `permissions: contents: read`, no secrets in the job, first-party publisher, private repo. Fix: pin the full commit SHA with the version in a comment.

- **A keep dir under `bin/`, `lib/` or `tests/` turns the gate red and keeps it red** — `tests/run:34` with `tests/run:42`. Measured from the copy's repo root with shellcheck on and `00-harness` as the only scenario: baseline `GATE: PASS ... shellcheck=ok (33 files)`; with `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP=tests/kept` `GATE: FAIL ... shellcheck=fail` on 6 findings in kept fixture files (5 SC2148, 1 SC2034); still FAIL on the next run with the variable unset; PASS again after removing the dir. `scripts/gate.sh` does `cd` to the repo root, so a relative value lands in the repo. A keep dir anywhere in the workdir also dirties the tree (exit 7 and receipt refusal per spec §3). Fix: say in the header that the dir must be outside the repo, or refuse a `KEEP` under `$REPO`.

- **`rm -rf "$KEEP/$name"` deletes whatever already has a scenario's name** — `tests/run:34`. Measured: a pre-existing `proj/01-s/notes` was deleted without notice; a `KEEP` that is a symlink is followed into its target, where same-named entries are replaced. Nothing marks a dir as created by `tests/run`, and the header does not say `<dir>/<name>` is replaced. Two runs sharing one keep dir clobber each other. In a world-writable parent another user can pre-place the keep path. A symlink at `$KEEP/<name>` is safe: the link is removed and the target stayed intact. Fix: document the replacement; optionally refuse a keep dir not owned by the caller.

- **`mkdir -p "$KEEP"` and `cd "$KEEP"` lack `--`** — `tests/run:19`. `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP=-` created a dir named `-`, then `cd -` went to `OLDPWD` and `KEEP` became two paths joined by a newline; scenario 1 ran, `mv` failed, exit 1, a work dir leaked in `/tmp`. `-rf` fails at `mkdir` before any scenario. Fix: `mkdir -p -- "$KEEP"; KEEP="$(cd -- "$KEEP" && pwd)"` (and `./` prefix or `cd -P` for the `-` case).

- **Artifact retention and empty-upload behaviour left at defaults** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml:45-48`. The repo's retention is 90 days (`gh api .../artifact-and-log-retention` returned `{"days":90}`). No `retention-days`, no `if-no-files-found`. Fix: `retention-days: 7` or similar.

- **`if: failure()` skips the hang case** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml:44`. A job that hits `timeout-minutes: 30` or is cancelled does not satisfy `failure()`, and the in-flight scenario's work dir is still under `/tmp`, not in the keep dir. A scenario that exceeds its own 300 s timeout is covered (measured: a 1 s timeout fixture was kept with its output). Fix: `if: ${{ !success() }}` if hang diagnosis matters.

- **Hidden files are dropped from the artifact; the comment says "every scenario's work dir"** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml:36` and `:45-48`. `include-hidden-files` defaults to `false` (action.yml lines 43-47), so every scenario repo's `.git` is excluded. That is safe for secrets and a loss for diagnosing `22-dirty-tree` and `40-receipt-required`. Job dirs are not hidden (`tests/lib.sh:23`: `test-<pid>-<s>/job`), so `run.log` is included. The tarball fix above resolves this too.

- **Upload follows symlinks** — the action's glob default is `followSymbolicLinks: true` (index.js:9770). Today the suite makes 2 symlinks, both to files in the repo (`tests/23-runner-lock.sh:26`, `tests/61-jev-pick.sh:57`), so nothing outside the repo is uploaded. A future scenario that links to `$HOME` or `/` would have the target's contents uploaded.

- **Pre-existing, not in this diff: shellcheck binary downloaded without a checksum** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml:21-22`. `curl ... | tar -xJ` then onto `PATH`; version-pinned, not hash-pinned. Fix: verify a SHA-256 before extracting.

- **Pre-existing, not in this diff: checkout keeps its token in `.git/config` while PR code runs** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml:16`. Read-only token, and the workspace is not part of the artifact. Fix: `persist-credentials: false`.

- **Pre-existing, not in this diff: the shellcheck verdict depends on the caller's cwd** — `tests/run:50`. Same copy, same fixture: `shellcheck=ok` from the repo root, `shellcheck=fail` with 4 SC2034 warnings from another directory (the `# shellcheck source=tests/lib.sh` directives resolve against cwd). CI and `scripts/gate.sh` both run from the root, so it does not bite today. Fix: `cd "$REPO"` around the shellcheck call or pass `-P "$REPO"`.

### Validated

- **Confirmed correct:**
  - Criterion 1, keep: fixture run with `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP=kept` gave `kept/01-ok/{out,cwd/made,cwd/link}` and `kept/02-bad/{out,cwd}`, per-scenario dirs mode `drwx------`, 0 entries left in a pinned `TMPDIR`, verdict unchanged (`GATE: FAIL passed=1 failed=1`).
  - Criterion 1, unset and empty string: 0 entries left in `TMPDIR`, same verdict and exit code.
  - Scenarios cannot see the variable: a fixture printed `seen=[unset]` (`tests/run:21`).
  - Early failure for a keep dir that cannot be made: `/proc/nope/x` and a path that is a file both exited 1 with 0 of 3 scenarios run (`tests/run:19`; errexit does apply inside the brace group).
  - Criterion 4: 7 of 7 mutants of `tests/run` are killed by `tests/00-harness.sh:22-37` (no removal when unset; no `unset`; no stale-dir removal; keep `out` only; copy instead of move; keep ignored; keep failed scenarios only). Unmutated: `GATE: PASS passed=1`.
  - Criterion 2, as written: `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP` is set at step level only (`ci.yml:35-37`), the upload step is gated by `if: failure()` (`ci.yml:44`), both use the same `${{ runner.temp }}/blast-off-tests` path, outside the workspace.
  - Criterion 3: header documents the variable (`tests/run:7-8`); the spec's `00-harness` row names it (`docs/spec.md:215`), and the row's three claims match what the test asserts.
  - No secret reaches the kept dirs or the artifact: `ci.yml` references no `secrets.*` and passes no token to the gate step; 14 scenarios export the literal `GH_TOKEN=dummy-not-a-token`; `tests/lib.sh:10` unsets the Jev keys; the fake `claude` records only `set`/`unset` (`tests/fakes/claude:34`) and a count (`:45`); the fake `jev` records a 6-character key prefix of a dummy (`tests/fakes/jev:12`); `start` prints names, never values. No scenario runs `env`/`printenv` into a file, and none creates a FIFO.
  - `permissions: contents: read` is unchanged and sufficient; the trigger is `pull_request`, not `pull_request_target`; the repo is private and not a fork.
  - `name` cannot be empty, `.`, `..` or contain `/` (glob `[0-9][0-9]-*.sh` at `tests/run:24`, `basename` at `:26`), so the `rm -rf` on line 34 cannot leave `$KEEP`.
  - A symlink planted at `$KEEP/<name>` is unlinked, not followed: the target dir kept its file.
  - Filenames written by scenarios, fakes and libs (tallied from redirect targets) contain none of the other rejected characters; the line feed at `22-dirty-tree.sh:123` is the only one found.

- **Examined, inconclusive:**
  - `.github/workflows/ci.yml:43-48` on GitHub: whether the step fails as the source says. Blocker: executing the action locally was denied; needs one red CI run or the command above.
  - `ci.yml:45`: whether v4 works when forced onto Node 24. Blocker: needs a real run. `checkout@v4` does (run 43778239611 is green under the same forcing).
  - `ci.yml:47`: whether a re-run attempt collides on the fixed artifact name `blast-off-tests`. Blocker: needs a re-run of a failed attempt.
  - `ci.yml:44`: that a job-level timeout reports as cancelled rather than failed. Blocker: stated from GitHub's documented behaviour, not observed here.
  - `tests/run:34` across filesystems: on hosted runners `/tmp` and `RUNNER_TEMP` should share a filesystem, so `mv` is a rename. Blocker: not checked on a runner.
  - The complete kept tree of a real full run (size, every filename). Blocker: the full suite was off limits; the filename check is static.

- **Not examined:**
  - `lib/*.sh` and `bin/blast-off` beyond grepping what they write into the job dir and `run.log`.
  - Scenarios `10` to `70` beyond the greps above and `22-dirty-tree.sh` lines 1-20 and 108-140.
  - `scripts/gate.sh` behaviour (read only), `README.md`, and the baton-runner planning files.

### Confidence

High on the `tests/run` and harness-test conclusions (all measured on a copy); medium-high on the upload failure (creation and rejection each verified, the action itself not run) — one deliberately red CI run would settle it. The advisor tool was rate-limited, so this had no second-reviewer pass. Left behind for inspection or deletion: `/tmp/bo-secrev.0MPqJG` (repo copy, mutants, the downloaded action source), and one work dir a mutant leaked in `/tmp` (probably `/tmp/tmp.lVl8pVVKXv`; I did not delete it because other `tmp.*` dirs there belong to concurrent runs).
